derived (hidden in the broadcast; the user's goal moment is the label frame)
rule: the puck stops against the back of the preview cage

limitations: PROPOSED rebuild from one broadcast camera; nothing is measured on the table.

Puck: the synthetic detector's track (data/games/nm26-semifinal/g2/puck-track-synth.json, PROPOSED, x/y = puck centre) where it has a detection, the hand readings (shots/edwall/puck-readings.json, z = 6 mm) elsewhere; low-score detections weigh less. The rest position is the mean of the detector's slow detections before the play (about 44 mm off the board; v1 snapped it to the board).

Right wing (passer) and centre (shooter): the lunges and turns are DESIGNED smootherstep moves fitted to the puck observations, the goal and the figures' own tracker v3 readings (src 0) inside the moves.

Both plays are modelled as heel-groove carries: the puck stays at the touching point of the figure from catch to release and leaves with that point's velocity (NTHF: 'carries the puck with the heel groove'). The fit penalises carries whose needed force lies outside the contact-normal fan (carry_force_check); the preview figure has no modelled groove.

The centre's shovel and the goal are hidden in the broadcast (behind the E goalie and the near goal frame): the shot is DESIGNED to score into the open far (+y) corner; its exact contact and line are not observed.
The other ten figures follow tracker v3 (data/games/nm26-semifinal/g2/figure-tracks-v3.json, PROPOSED, not verified frame by frame).
Ice friction 926.1 mm/s^2 is borrowed from the spjass slide fit; figure restitution 0.5 frictionless; puck thickness 12 mm assumed.
